{
  "findings": [

      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 182,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "BasePaginator can pass negative offsets to Django queryset slicing",
      "body": "The new slicing logic keeps cursor.offset unchanged when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor offsets are parsed from client-supplied cursor strings and can be negative. A previous-page cursor such as 0:-1:1 will cause queryset[start_offset:stop] to be evaluated with a negative start or stop. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and will raise an error, so endpoints using BasePaginator can be made to return 500s. Even if negative slicing were emulated, it would not provide the intended pagination semantics. Offsets should be validated or clamped to non-negative values before slicing."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator intentionally uses unsupported negative QuerySet slices",
      "body": "When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator sets start_offset to that negative value and slices the queryset with it. Django ORM does not support negative slicing; this will raise an error for the new audit-log optimized path whenever an advanced user sends a negative-offset cursor. The comment claiming the underlying ORM handles negative slicing is incorrect. Negative offsets should be rejected as invalid pagination input."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py",
      "line": 79,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering used for audit logs",
      "body": "The endpoint orders audit logs by -datetime but uses OptimizedCursorPaginator, whose get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the ordered field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object, so any optimized_pagination=true request that returns at least one row will raise TypeError while building the cursor. A datetime-aware paginator, or an optimized paginator implementing DateTimePaginator-style key conversion, is required."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/utils/cursors.py",
      "line": 28,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Cursor offsets are accepted as arbitrary signed integers",
      "body": "Cursor.__init__ casts offset to int without validating that it is non-negative, and Cursor.from_string therefore accepts negative offsets from query parameters. The pagination changes in this PR expose or rely on negative offsets, but Django queryset pagination cannot handle them. This creates a client-controlled path to invalid paginator state and server errors. Unless a paginator explicitly supports signed offsets, cursor offsets should be validated and negative values rejected."
    },

      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Extra-row trimming logic is incorrect for negative offsets",
      "body": "In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, after slicing with a negative offset, the code tests len(results) == offset + limit + extra to decide whether to drop the extra sentinel row. With a negative offset, this expected length is wrong and can be non-positive, so the sentinel row may not be removed or the result set may be trimmed incorrectly if negative slicing were ever supported. This can produce incorrect page contents and wrong next/prev cursor flags."

Without tests, the datetime incompatibility and negative-slicing regressions are easy to ship."

findings.title: BasePaginator can pass negative offsets to Django queryset slicing
findings.body: The new slicing logic keeps cursor.offset unchanged when cursor.is_prev is true. Cursor offsets are parsed from client-supplied cursor strings and can be negative. A previous-page cursor such as 0:-1:1 will cause queryset[start_offset:stop] to be evaluated with a negative start or stop. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and will raise an error, so endpoints using BasePaginator can be made to return 500s. Even if negative slicing were emulated, it would not provide the intended pagination semantics. Offsets should be validated or clamped to non-negative values before slicing.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator intentionally uses unsupported negative QuerySet slices
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator sets start_offset to that negative value and slices the queryset with it. Django ORM does not support negative slicing; this will raise an error for the new audit-log optimized path whenever an advanced user sends a negative-offset cursor. The comment claiming the underlying ORM handles negative slicing is incorrect. Negative offsets should be rejected as invalid pagination input.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with datetime ordering used for audit logs
findings.body: The endpoint orders audit logs by -datetime but uses OptimizedCursorPaginator, whose get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the ordered field value. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime object, so any optimized_pagination=true request that returns at least one row will raise TypeError while building the cursor. A datetime-aware paginator, or an optimized paginator implementing DateTimePaginator-style key conversion, is required.

findings.title: Cursor offsets are accepted as arbitrary signed integers
findings.body: Cursor.__init__ casts offset to int without validating that it is non-negative, and Cursor.from_string therefore accepts negative offsets from query parameters. The pagination changes in this PR expose or rely on negative offsets, but Django queryset pagination cannot handle them. This creates a client-controlled path to invalid paginator state and server errors. Unless a paginator explicitly supports signed offsets, cursor offsets should be validated and negative values rejected.

findings.title: Extra-row trimming logic is incorrect for negative offsets
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, after slicing with a negative offset, the code tests len(results) == offset + limit + extra to decide whether to drop the extra sentinel row. With a negative offset, this expected length is wrong and can be non-positive, so the sentinel row may not be removed or the result set may be trimmed incorrectly if negative slicing were ever supported. This can produce incorrect page contents and wrong next/prev cursor flags.

findings.title: No tests cover the new optimized pagination path
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator, a query-parameter opt-in, permission gating, and negative-offset handling, but no tests are included. Tests are needed for the audit-log endpoint with optimized_pagination enabled, datetime cursor generation, negative or invalid cursor offsets, and fallback behavior for non-privileged users. Without tests, the datetime incompatibility and negative-slicing regressions are easy to ship.
